narrative.overview: India Pulse posts the country's street-level prices the way a fuel station posts its rates. Green canopy fascia runs across the top, cool white enamel panels sit below, and every price sits in a dark window with light, heavy, condensed digits that are revised in place each morning. The system serves a trader scanning before the open, so density and alignment come before decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Prices in fixed-width green digit windows, aligned within each board.
One reserved accent: signal saffron marks the selected city and nothing else.
Line form carries data state: solid means observed, dashed means reconstructed.
Flat enamel: no shadows, gradients or glow.

rules.name: The Reserved Saffron Rule
rules.body: Signal saffron means "your city". Any other use of saffron, or a tint of it, breaks the rule; alerts use the rise family instead.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number on screen uses tabular figures, so digits line up down a column.

rules.name: The Enamel Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat painted enamel: no bevels, gradients, glows or blur.

dos: Do put every headline price in a digit window and keep windows the same width within a board.
Do name the unit and the source in every board header.
Do draw reconstructed history dashed and say so in the chart legend.
Do use rise (#a8321d) and fall (#1e5fa0) for change, and slate for no change.
donts: Don't use saffron for anything but the selected city and the canopy band.
Don't render digits as glowing LEDs or add neon, glass or gradients.
Don't fall back to KPI cards with floating sparklines; values live in board rows.
Don't mark selection with a colored side stripe.
